name: Egocentric 2D Hand Pose Benchmark
description: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video has broad implications across various domains, including human-computer interaction, assistive technologies, activity recognition, and robotics, making it a topic of significant research interest. The efficacy of modern machine learning models depends on the quality of data used for their training. Thus, this work is devoted to the analysis of state-of-the-art egocentric datasets suitable for 2D hand pose estimation. We propose a novel protocol for dataset evaluation, which encompasses not only the analysis of stated dataset characteristics and assessment of data quality, but also the identification of dataset shortcomings through the evaluation of state-of-the-art hand pose estimation models. Our study reveals that despite the availability of numerous egocentric databases intended for 2D hand pose estimation, the majority are tailored for specific use cases. There is no ideal benchmark dataset yet; however, H2O and GANerated Hands datasets emerge as the most promising real and synthetic datasets, respectively.
reputation: A focused survey-style benchmark used by the hand-pose community to compare egocentric datasets and methods; influential for dataset analysis but no single dominant standard dataset exists.
notes: Non-LLM computer-vision benchmark; datasets vary in size and domain specificity (many are task-specific), potential dataset shortcomings and domain gaps noted by the authors; risk of small/biased subsets and lack of a single unified benchmark.
